entries.issuing_body: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), U.S. Department of the Treasury
entries.title: FinCEN Minnesota Geographic Targeting Order published in the Federal Register, effective August 11, 2026 through February 6, 2027
entries.facts: FinCEN's Geographic Targeting Order requiring banks and money transmitters located in Hennepin County and Ramsey County, Minnesota to retain and report records of certain funds transfers of $3,000 or more was published in the Federal Register on August 11, 2026 as a Rule (91 FR 51588, document 2026-16365, 31 CFR part 1010). The order states that its terms "are effective on August 11, 2026, and end on February 6, 2027," and that the action is taken "in furtherance of Treasury's efforts to combat international money laundering relating to government benefits fraud in Minnesota." A Covered Business is any bank as defined in 31 CFR 1010.100(d) or money transmitter as defined in 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5) with a branch, subsidiary or office in the two counties. Covered Transactions are funds transfers where the originator or transmittor gives an address in the covered area, is not a public company and is not a BSA-regulated financial institution, and where the beneficiary or the beneficiary's financial institution is located outside the United States. Reports are filed through FinCEN's Financial Industry Portal as CSV files by the end of the month following the month of the transaction. Money transmitters must report "the form of transmittal (wire, convertible virtual currency transmission, ledger entry, or other)" and, for ledger entries tracking credits and debits with hawaladars located internationally, whether cash couriers are used to settle those debits. Records must be retained for five years, and the order states that a Covered Business and its officers, directors, employees and agents "may be liable, without limitation, for civil or criminal penalties for willfully violating any of the terms of this Order."
entries.relevant_to: money transmitters, banks, payment platforms, convertible virtual currency businesses operating in Minnesota

entries.title: CFTC Federal Register notice: Innovation Advisory Committee meets August 20 on crypto assets, AI and prediction markets; written statements due August 27
entries.facts: The CFTC published a notice of meeting in the Federal Register on August 11, 2026 (91 FR 51697, document 2026-16328) announcing that its Innovation Advisory Committee will hold an in-person meeting for members on August 20, 2026 from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time, with the public able to attend virtually. The notice states: "At this meeting, the IAC will discuss topics including crypto assets, artificial intelligence, and prediction markets, along with recent CFTC activity in these markets." The DATES section states that "Members of the public who wish to submit written statements in connection with the meeting should submit them by Thursday, August 27, 2026," and comments may be submitted through Regulations.gov, by mail or by hand delivery to the Secretary of the Commission. Registration is not required, call-in details and a live webcast on cftc.gov are provided, and a transcript will be published after the meeting. The notice is dated August 7, 2026 and signed by Christopher Kirkpatrick, Secretary of the Commission.
entries.source_label: Federal Register, 91 FR 51697 (CFTC Notice of Meeting, doc. 2026-16328)
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, crypto exchanges, derivatives intermediaries, fintech firms

entries.issuing_body: United States Senate (Senate Daily Press Gallery floor log)
entries.title: Senate floor log: cloture motion on H.R. 3633, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, ripens Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 2:15 p.m.
entries.facts: The Senate Daily Press Gallery floor log for Monday, August 10, 2026 records that the Senate convened for a pro forma session at 10:00 a.m., that Senator Boozman presided and that no business was conducted, and lists further pro forma sessions with no business expected on August 13, 17, 20, 24, 27 and 31 and on September 1, 4, 8 and 10. The log states: "The Senate returns for business on Monday, September 14th at 3:00 p.m. At that time, following any Leader remarks, the Senate will be in a period of morning business. At approximately 5:30 p.m. the Senate will vote on cloture on Executive Calendar #902, Matthew Byrne to be a US District Judge for the Southern District of Ohio." It adds: "Please note: the cloture motion with respect to H.R.3633 - Digital Asset Market Clarity Act will ripen on Tuesday, September 15th at 2:15 p.m." The Gallery's standing schedule line states that "Except for pro forma sessions, the Senate stands adjourned until 3.00 p.m. on Monday, September 14th."
entries.source_label: U.S. Senate Daily Press Gallery, floor log for Monday, August 10, 2026
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, token issuers, custodians, digital-asset market participants

entries.issuing_body: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Kentucky
entries.title: DOJ: Mexican "money broker" pleads guilty to laundering more than $1.9 million in drug proceeds returned via cryptocurrency or wire transfers
entries.facts: The Department of Justice announced on August 7, 2026 (Press Release 26-905) that Daniel Gordiano Valenzuela, 60, a Mexican national, pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy. According to the release, he "served as a 'money broker' in an organization that conspired with drug traffickers to launder money for them in Mexico" and "personally arranged for the laundering of $1, 973,076 from the sale of drugs and used a network of co-conspirators to pick up the drug proceeds throughout the United States." The release states: "After delivery of the bulk cash, he provided instructions for the transfer of those funds via cryptocurrency or wire transfer and then received a 'commission,' or percentage of the money laundered successfully." Sentencing is scheduled for November 19 and he faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. The case was investigated by the DEA Detroit Field Division and IRS Criminal Investigation Detroit and is prosecuted by the Criminal Division's Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section and the Eastern District of Kentucky.
entries.source_label: U.S. Department of Justice press release 26-905
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, money services businesses, AML and financial-crime compliance teams
